content.title: Fully differentiable model discovery
content.abstract: Model discovery aims at autonomously discovering differential equations underlying a dataset. Approaches based on Physics Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have shown great promise, but a fully-differentiable model which explicitly learns the equation has remained elusive. In this paper we propose such an approach by integrating neural network-based surrogates with Sparse Bayesian Learning (SBL). This combination yields a robust model discovery algorithm, which we showcase on various datasets. We then identify a connection with multitask learning, and build on it to construct a Physics Informed Normalizing Flows (PINFs). We present a proof-of-concept using a PINF to directly learn a density model from single particle data. Our work expands PINNs to various types of neural network architectures, and connects neural network-based surrogates to the rich field of Bayesian parameter inference.
content.one-sentence_summary: We show how to do differentiable model discovery.
